title: Park Shift: Ride-Operations Simulator
description:
A first-person co-op game about running a theme park attraction from the operator's side: open the shift, load guests, verify restraints, dispatch trains, keep two trains moving through block zones and recover from faults before the 3-minute shift ends.

Why I built it: I operate and troubleshoot real attractions, so I wanted to model ride control logic in software the same way a PLC program and an HMI split the work.

How it works
- The simulation core (state machine, block zones, two-train logic, guest queue, 6-fault catalog, scoring, telemetry) is pure C# with no Unity references. Unity is only the presentation layer.
- Every player action goes through one validated command path, so the same rules run in solo play and on a multiplayer host.
- Faults have recovery steps, including a lockout-gated maintenance reset that needs the Technician role.
- 9 automated tests plus a scripted full-shift bot playtest found and fixed two logic bugs (a staged train that never advanced, and an unfair instant stacking fault).

Stack: Unity 6, C#, FishNet (co-op scaffold). Built with AI coding agents (Claude, Claude Code); I designed the systems and test it in Unity.
tasks: Engine-agnostic simulation core (state machine, block zones, two trains)
Six-fault catalog with recovery steps, incl. lockout-gated reset
Fix staged-train progress bug and stacking-fault grace period
Prefab-aware scene builder for real art
Replace primitives with CC0 art packs
update: Vertical slice playable in Unity: full 3-minute shift with dispatch, block zones and six faults. Core sim passes 9 tests and a bot playtest.

title: BlasterBlast: Mixed-Reality Target Blaster
description:
A mixed-reality shooting gallery for Meta Quest 3S. Pop-up targets appear on the room's real walls, the right controller is a blaster with a laser, haptics and 3D sound, and a show-style state machine runs each round (Idle, Countdown, Running, Results).

Why I built it: I maintain interactive blaster attractions at work and wanted to understand the mixed-reality side end to end.

Design
- Targets register themselves with the game manager, so the game doesn't care whether the room scan (MR Utility Kit) or a fallback spawner placed them.
- Standard, bonus and "don't shoot" decoy targets, a streak multiplier and an S/A/B/C grade.
- Every raise, hit, miss and escape is logged to CSV and charted in Python to tune difficulty, the same idea as trending a fault log.

Status: passthrough runs on the headset; the gameplay scripts are written and being wired up and tested on the Quest.

Stack: Unity 6, Meta XR SDK, OpenXR, MR Utility Kit, C#, PowerShell build tools, Python/matplotlib, built with Claude Code.
tasks: Unity 6 + Meta XR SDK + Android build setup
Passthrough MR running on the Quest 3S
Gameplay scripts: round state machine, targets, raycast blaster, haptics, telemetry
Wire the scene and test a full round on the headset
Spawn targets on real walls with MR Utility Kit
Gameplay pack: bonus/decoy targets, hit FX, sounds
update: Milestone 1: passthrough mixed reality running on the Quest 3S. Next: targets on real walls.

title: BuildVault: Maker Project Hub
description:
The site you're on. A full-stack app where makers document builds: projects with BOMs, tasks and progress bars, file and video uploads, dated progress updates, follows, boosts, a community forum, a parts inventory with CSV import, and a focus timer with streaks.

How it's built
- React 19 + Vite frontend, Node/Express 5 API, SQLite, Clerk authentication.
- Self-hosted on my own Ubuntu VPS behind nginx with Let's Encrypt, run as a systemd service.
- One-command deploy script: database backup, pull, build, restart, health check.

Security and quality pass (Oct 2026): I had independent AI review agents audit the code, then fixed what they found: private-data leaks, an upload path that could have run scripts, unscoped updates, and a schema that only existed on the server. Automated API tests now cover those fixes.

Built with AI coding agents (Claude, Clawbot); I set the scope, reviewed the changes and run the server.
tasks: Projects, BOM, tasks, files, progress updates
Feed, follows, boosts, community forum, notifications
Inventory with CSV import and review step
Deploy on Ubuntu VPS: nginx, SSL, systemd
Public portfolio profile with featured projects
update: Security and portfolio update: public profiles, featured projects, video playback, and automated API tests.

title: AI Missing-Persons Registry
description:
A humanitarian prototype for finding people after a disaster, when lists of missing and found people get shared as photos of handwritten and printed pages.

What it does
- AI reads names and details from photos of lists and turns them into structured records.
- Records are de-duplicated and cross-referenced, and the data model follows PFIF 1.4 so it could be exchanged with other registries.
- Trust model: the AI only ranks possible matches; a person reviews and confirms every match before anything is marked as found.

Status: extraction and matching validated on test data only (no real personal data).

Stack: Next.js, Supabase, an AI vision model, built with AI coding agents.
tasks: AI extraction of names from photos
Human review gate for every match
update: Extraction and matching working on test data. AI ranks, people confirm.

title: Clawbot: Self-Hosted AI Agent
description:
My always-on AI assistant, reachable from Telegram and running on my own Linux VPS through the OpenClaw agent framework on the Claude API.

What it does
- Several agents with separate roles and their own Telegram bots, including one that works on this website's code.
- Has edited and deployed BuildVault directly on the server; it now follows a git workflow where GitHub is the source of truth and every deploy backs up the database first.

Ops lessons: I debugged an outage where the bot stopped answering. The cause was a provider billing cooldown stored in its config plus a fallback model that didn't exist. I cleared the cooldown, confirmed the API worked directly, and brought it back online; fixing the fallback model is next.

Stack: Linux (Ubuntu), OpenClaw, Claude API, Telegram Bot API, systemd.
tasks: Deploy agent gateway on Ubuntu VPS
Use it to build and deploy BuildVault
Git-first workflow + DB backups on deploy
update: Now deploys BuildVault through a git workflow with automatic database backups.

title: ESP32 LED Matrix Controller
description:
An ESP32 controller for a 16x16 WS2812B (NeoPixel) LED panel with a Wi-Fi web interface to change patterns and colors from a phone.

- Firmware in C++ (Arduino framework) on the ESP32.
- Web UI served by the ESP32 itself over Wi-Fi.

Photos and a video of the panel running are coming.

title: 120 VAC Sleep-Mode Control Circuit
description:
An Arduino-based control circuit that switches a 120 VAC load into a timed sleep mode, with the RF remote simulated during development.

It's the same idea as a retrofit I designed at work: remote relay control wired in parallel with the existing manual switch, so manual control always stays available as a backup.
